per_case.answer: Chickenpox is a common and extremely infectious childhood disease that also affects adults on occasion. It is also known as varicella [1].

Antibiotics are ineffective against chickenpox because it is a viral disease [1]. Additionally, it is stated that "Antibiotics are ineffective against viruses, though antiviral drugs exist for some viruses, including chickenpox" [2].
A single attack of chickenpox almost always confers lifelong immunity against the disease [1].

Cirrhosis is a chronic, degenerative disease in which normal liver cells are damaged and are then replaced by scar tissue [1]. It changes the structure of the liver and the blood vessels that nourish it, reducing the liver's ability to manufacture proteins and process hormones, nutrients, medications, and poisons [1].

Conjunctivitis is the inflammation of the conjunctiva, a thin, delicate membrane that covers the eyeball and lines the eyelid [1]. It is also described as an inflammation or redness of the lining of the white part of the eye and the underside of the eyelid [3].

Conjunctivitis can be caused by a viral infection, such as a cold, acute respiratory infection, or diseases like measles, herpes simplex, or herpes zoster [1]. It can also be caused by exposure to hazards like wind, smoke, dust, and allergic reactions caused by pollen, dust, or grass [2]. Additionally, problems with inadequate drainage of the tear ducts and exposure to sun lamps or electrical arcs used during welding can cause conjunctivitis [2].

Dementia is defined as a loss of mental ability severe enough to interfere with normal activities of daily living, lasting more than six months, not present since birth, and not associated with a loss or alteration of consciousness [3].

Cancer is caused by substances in the environment that induce mutations, with prolonged exposure [1]. Malignant cells have been altered such that a person is more likely to develop cancer, but only if they also have prolonged exposure to intensive sunlight [2].
No, cancer is not a single disease. According to passage [1], "Cancer is not just one disease, but a large group of almost one hundred diseases."

Celiac disease is a disease of the digestive system that damages the small intestine and interferes with the absorption of nutrients from food [1]. It is an autoimmune disorder that occurs when the body reacts abnormally to gluten, a protein found in wheat, rye, barley, and possibly oats [3]. This reaction causes an inflammatory response in the small intestine, leading to impaired nutrient absorption and wide-ranging problems in many systems of the body [3].

Croup is a common childhood ailment, a mild viral infection of the larynx [1], also known as laryngotracheitis, which describes the inflammation of the trachea and larynx [1]. The typical root cause of the infection is Parainfluenza viruses [1], but influenza (flu) and cold viruses may sometimes be responsible [1].
The most striking feature of diphtheria is the formation of a grayish membrane covering the tonsils and upper part of the throat, as stated in passage [1].
Diphtheria usually involves the nose, throat, and air passages [1]. It can also affect the upper throat (pharynx) [3], the voice box (larynx) [3], and the nervous system [2].

Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an inherited disease that affects the lungs, digestive system, sweat glands, and male fertility [1]. It affects the body's ability to move salt and water in and out of cells, causing the lungs and pancreas to secrete thick mucus [1].

Colic is persistent, unexplained crying in a healthy baby between two weeks and five months of age [1]. It is not a disease, affects 10–20% of all infants, and is more common in boys than in girls [1].
Constipation is defined as an acute or chronic condition in which bowel movements occur less often than usual or consist of hard, dry stools that are painful or difficult to pass [1, 2, 3].
An adult who has not had a bowel movement in three days is considered constipated [1].

Depressive disorders are mental illnesses characterized by a profound and persistent feeling of sadness or despair and/or a loss of interest in things that were once pleasurable [2]. Disturbance in sleep, appetite, and mental processes are a common accompaniment [2]. Changes in the levels of certain neurotransmitters, such as serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine, are thought to be related to depressive disorders [3].

Carpal tunnel syndrome is a disorder caused by compression at the wrist of the median nerve supplying the hand, causing numbness and tingling [1]. It is characterized by the compression of the median nerve in the wrist, which can cause the hand to feel as if it has "gone to sleep" [2].

A concussion is a trauma-induced change in mental status, with confusion and amnesia, and with or without a brief loss of consciousness [1]. It occurs when the head hits or is hit by an object, or when the brain is jarred against the skull, with sufficient force to cause temporary loss of function in the higher centers of the brain [1].

A cough is a forceful release of air from the lungs [4]. It serves a protective function by clearing the respiratory system of irritants and secretions [1]. This helps to protect the respiratory system by removing harmful substances and aiding in the body's defense against infective agents and irritants [2].

Dehydration is the loss of water and salts essential for normal body function [1]. It occurs when the body loses more fluid than it takes in [3]. This condition can result from various causes, including illness, hot and dry climate, not drinking enough water, and overuse of diuretics or other medications [3].

Contact dermatitis is the name for any skin inflammation that occurs when the skin's surface comes in contact with a substance originating outside the body [1]. It is the most common skin condition requiring medical attention and the foremost source of work-related disease [1]. Contact dermatitis is an allergic reaction to something that irritates the skin and is manifested by one or more lines of red, swollen, blistered skin that may itch or burn [2].
There are two kinds of contact dermatitis: irritant and allergic. This is stated in passage [1] as "There are two kinds of contact dermatitis, irritant and allergic."
Down syndrome is the most common cause of mental retardation and malformation in a newborn [2]. It occurs because of the presence of an extra chromosome [2].

Dyslexia is a learning disability characterized by problems in reading, spelling, writing, speaking, or listening [2]. It is a condition where people have trouble learning early reading skills, problems hearing individual sounds in words, analyzing whole words in parts, and blending sounds into words [4]. Dyslexia is not a disease, but rather a different kind of mind that learns in a different way from other people [1].

Endometriosis is a condition in which bits of the tissue similar to the lining of the uterus (endometrium) grow in other parts of the body [1]. This tissue builds up and sheds in response to monthly hormonal changes, and is sometimes said to look like "powder burns" [2].
Botulism antitoxin is given to adults if it can be administered within 72 hours after symptoms are first observed [2]. If given later, it provides no benefit.
When breathing is impaired in botulism, patients are put on a mechanical ventilator to assist their breathing [1].
Folic acid deficiency results in anemia characterized by red blood cells that are large in size but few in number [2]. This type of anemia is one of the most common of all vitamin deficiencies [2].
The chickenpox rash typically lasts about a week [1].
Applying wet compresses or bathing the child in cool or lukewarm water once a day can help the itch [1].
According to the CONTEXT, in cirrhosis, damaged liver cells are replaced by scar tissue [1].

Cold sores usually appear on or around the lips [1]. They most often occur on the lips, which distinguishes them from canker sores [1]. In 95% of patients with cold sores, the blisters occur at the outer edge of the lips, also known as the "vermilion border" [3].
According to [2], dementia is not associated with a loss or alteration of consciousness.
Celiac disease damages the small intestine and interferes with the absorption of nutrients from food [1]. It specifically interferes with the body's ability to absorb nutrients from foods [2].

Croup is usually not serious, and most children recover within a few days [1]. In fact, it is described as a "temporary condition" and children typically recover completely within three to six days [3].
The name 'cystic fibrosis' derives from the fibrous scar tissue that develops in the pancreas, one of the principal organs affected by the disease [1].

Infant colic typically occurs between two weeks and five months of age [1]. Symptoms usually appear when a baby is 14–21 days old, reach a crescendo at the age of three months, and disappear within the next eight weeks [1].

Yes, diphtheria can be fatal. According to passage [1], the mortality rate varies from 1.5–25% in countries without routine immunization. Passage [2] also states that obstruction of the airway may result in respiratory compromise and death.
The median nerve is compressed in carpal tunnel syndrome [2].

A concussion may be accompanied by the following symptoms: 
- confusion [1]
- dizziness [1]
- vacant stare or confused expression [1]
- incoherent or incomprehensible speech [1]
- incoordination or weakness [1]
- amnesia for the events immediately preceding the blow [1]
- nausea or vomiting [1]
- double vision [1]
- ringing in the ears [1]
- headache [3]
- disorientation as to time, date, or place [3]
- confusion [3]
- anxiety [4]
- depression [4]
- sleep disturbances [4]
- light and noise intolerance [4]
Coughing is considered protective because it clears the respiratory system of irritants and secretions [1]. This helps the body in clearing respiratory system of infective agents and irritants [2].

According to the CONTEXT, dehydration occurs when the body loses more fluid than it takes in [1]. This condition can result from various causes, including not drinking enough water, overuse of diuretics or other medications that increase urination, and excessive urination (polyuria) [2]. The body's fluid supply is severely depleted during dehydration, which can lead to complications such as hypovolemic shock [4].

Glucose cannot be absorbed into cells in diabetes mellitus because most cells are unable to transport glucose into the cell without the presence of insulin [2]. When there is not enough insulin produced or when the doorway no longer recognizes the insulin key, glucose stays in the blood rather entering the cells [4].
Down syndrome is caused by an extra copy or a rearrangement of chromosome 21 [2].

Yes, dyslexia is often inherited. According to [1], research suggests that the condition is often inherited, and [2] states that in many cases, dyslexia appears to be inherited. Additionally, [3] mentions that previous studies have pointed out linkages of other potential dyslexia genes to chromosomes, suggesting a genetic component to the condition.

The displaced tissue in endometriosis grows and sheds each month during a woman's menstrual cycle, similar to the tissue lining the uterus [1]. This means that the displaced tissue, like the endometrium, grows and is shed during the menstrual cycle.
Cold sores are caused by a herpes simplex virus infection [3]. The herpes simplex virus is a member of the human herpes viruses [1].
Red blood cells in folic acid deficiency anemia are large in size but few in number [1].

According to the CONTEXT, chickenpox is a "common and extremely infectious childhood disease" [1]. This suggests that chickenpox is indeed contagious. Additionally, it is stated that "almost every case of chickenpox, no matter how mild, leads to lifelong protection against further attacks" [3], implying that the disease is easily spread.
Cirrhosis is a chronic, degenerative disease [1]. It gets worse over time and can become potentially life threatening [1].

According to the CONTEXT, reduced mental ability must last more than six months to be considered dementia. This is stated in passage [1] as "lasting more than six months" and also in passage [2] as "lasting six months or more."

According to the CONTEXT, if cancer cells have spread to the surrounding tissues, then even after the malignant tumor is removed, it generally recurs [1]. This suggests that the key danger described for cancer cells spreading is their ability to recur after removal, likely due to the initial mutation in the DNA caused by environmental factors, such as carcinogens [1].

Celiac disease damages the small intestine and interferes with the absorption of nutrients from food, which suggests that it affects the digestive system [1]. Additionally, the inflammation and malabsorption caused by celiac disease create wide-ranging problems in many systems of the body [2].

Cystic fibrosis affects the digestive system [1], sweat glands [1], and male fertility [2]. It also affects female fertility, particularly during puberty, due to poor nutrition or chronic lung infection [4].

No, infant colic is not associated with an unhealthy baby. According to passage [1], colic is described as "persistent, unexplained crying in a healthy baby between two weeks and five months of age." This suggests that colic is a condition that affects healthy infants, rather than those who are unhealthy.

Disturbance in sleep, appetite, and mental processes are common accompaniments of depressive disorders besides sadness [1]. Other symptoms include sudden loss of appetite or compulsive eating, inability to concentrate, and lack of trust or fear someone they know well [2].

Carpal tunnel syndrome causes numbness, burning, tingling, and a prickly pin-like sensation over the palm surface of the hand, and into the thumb, forefinger, middle finger, and half of the ring finger. Some individuals also notice a shooting pain which goes from the wrist up the arm, or down into the hand and fingers [1].

Yes, contact dermatitis can be triggered by substances outside the body. According to passage [1], contact dermatitis is the name for any skin inflammation that occurs when the skin's surface comes in contact with a substance originating outside the body.
